report: Independent Audit Evidence - Zero Trust Re-validation

critical_defects_found.title: GraphQL me query broken - JWT format mismatch
critical_defects_found.detail: Phase 3 auth service creates JWT with 'userId' claim, NestJS JWT strategy reads 'payload.sub' -> undefined -> PrismaError(500). All GraphQL authenticated queries fail.
critical_defects_found.fix: Added 'sub: payload.userId' to createToken() in shared/security.js

critical_defects_found.title: Mass assignment vulnerability - role escalation
critical_defects_found.detail: Registration endpoint accepts 'role' from request body, allowing arbitrary role assignment (e.g. ADMIN). Attacker can register as admin.
critical_defects_found.fix: Removed 'role' from destructured body, hardcoded to 'CHILD'

critical_defects_found.title: Rate limit bypass via X-Forwarded-For spoofing
critical_defects_found.detail: bruteForceProtect uses req.ip which can be spoofed via X-Forwarded-For header. Attackers can rotate IP headers to bypass rate limits.
critical_defects_found.mitigation: Documented. Production should use real IP from proxy trust or connection.remoteAddress.

notable_observations: GraphQL stack traces exposed (development mode). Will be suppressed in production with NODE_ENV=production.
All 5 services have SIGTERM/SIGINT signal handlers
22 cross-service dependencies are all through /shared modules (good isolation)
Only 2 unit test files for the NestJS API
No eval(), no empty catch blocks, no real secrets in code
